issue_context.title: Taiko spinners stutter when using classic or imported skins
issue_context.body:
### Type

Performance

### Bug description

1. Select "classic" or an imported skin
2. Play a taiko map containing a spinner

Right before the spinner comes on-screen the game with freeze for a split second.

### Screenshots or videos

https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/17962514/227799859-1bd80879-2531-42b7-9198-0f06f7fcf5c5.mp4



### Version

2023.326.1-lazer

comments: for me, the stutter is more intense, freezing sometimes up to an entire second
From what I can tell this only applies to the first spinner/swell in a beatmap.

review_comments:
This code as written currently crashes for me when trying to start an osu! map. It does so because:

1. Rulesets will attempt to load framework shaders (because they can't see the game-global shader manager, they see the ruleset shader manager)
2. Upon doing so, they will hit the `base.Load()` call here
3. `base.Load()` internally calls `LoadRaw()`
4. `LoadRaw()` can't read framework resources, so it helpfully returns null source
5.
```
System.ArgumentNullException: Value cannot be null. (Parameter 'source')
   at Vortice.D3DCompiler.Compiler.Compile(ReadOnlySpan`1 source, ShaderMacro[] defines, Include include, String entryPoint, String sourceName, String profile, ShaderFlags shaderFlags, Blob& blob, Blob& errorBlob)
   at Veldrid.D3D11.D3D11Shader.CompileCode(ShaderDescription description)
   at Veldrid.D3D11.D3D11Shader..ctor(ID3D11Device device, ShaderDescription description)
   at Veldrid.D3D11.D3D11ResourceFactory.CreateShaderCore(ShaderDescription& description)
   at Veldrid.ResourceFactory.CreateShader(ShaderDescription& description)
   at Veldrid.ResourceFactory.CreateShader(ShaderDescription description)
   at osu.Framework.Graphics.Veldrid.Shaders.VeldridShader.loadToGpu() in D:\Open Source\osu-framework\osu.Framework\Graphics\Veldrid\Shaders\VeldridShader.cs:line 214
```

This can be avoided by also overriding `LoadRaw()` to try the parent, too - but, more importantly, wasn't the goal here to *avoid* recompiling the game-global shaders? As is they will get recompiled every play anyway because every play is a fresh instance of `RulesetShaderManager`, and the base call comes first. What am I missing here?

I'm quite confused. How are you seeing the crash? Are you potentially running in debug with "throw on caught exceptions" turned on or something like that?

There should be a try-catch which falls back to the parent (global) shader manager. Each `ShaderManager` has its own cache, so when falling back, there would be no recompilation as it is cached at that level.

As such, overriding `LoadRaw` should not be required.

I just did a framework checkout and ran the game in debug. I didn't touch any other settings. Is that an invalid way to test?

This was on windows/veldrid+dx11, if it matters.

Are you able to provide a full call stack of the crash? Is it somehow happening outside the `try-catch` in this PR?

I can't repro any crash locally, unfortunately..

Very interesting. That might be D3D specific, but it does reveal that we are still attempting to load a shader to the GPU even after it fails to compile, which is a large oversight.

https://github.com/ppy/osu-framework/blob/e84265d661847a21fbf27875f3528f35f209bf2d/osu.Framework/Graphics/Veldrid/Shaders/VeldridShader.cs#L202-L205

This probably needs to throw rather than gracefully being caught and continuing with execution.

Or at very least, the scheduled gpu upload should be omitted in fail cases.
I've made adjustments to the framework-side PR to address the issue you found. Turns out I can reproduce it with metal renderer, and was using legacy GL when testing this PR.
Tested with latest framework changes, looks good now 👍
